questions.prompt: Which file configures a WebdriverIO test runner project?
questions.explanation: The WDIO testrunner reads wdio.conf.(js|ts) for specs, capabilities, framework, services and reporters.

questions.prompt: In modern WebdriverIO, commands such as `$('#login').click()` are asynchronous and must be awaited.
questions.explanation: WebdriverIO v8 and later removed the synchronous mode (based on node-fibers), so commands return Promises and need await.
$ returns one element (the first match); $$ returns an array-like collection of all matches.
Without await, getText() returns a pending Promise, so console.log prints the Promise rather than the text. Adding await gives the text.

questions.prompt: This check fails randomly because the toast takes a moment to appear. What is the best fix?
options: Use the WebdriverIO expect matcher, which retries: await expect($('.toast')).toHaveText('Saved')
Use a try/catch around the assertion
questions.explanation: expect-webdriverio matchers wait and retry until the condition is met or the wait timeout elapses. pause() is a fixed sleep.

questions.prompt: Which can WebdriverIO drive? Select all that apply.
options: Desktop browsers via WebDriver or WebDriver BiDi
Unit-test components in a real browser (component testing)
questions.explanation: WebdriverIO supports browsers, mobile via Appium and component testing in the browser runner. It has no mainframe terminal support.

questions.prompt: What is a WebdriverIO custom command typically used for?
options: Adding a reusable action to browser or element objects, e.g. browser.addCommand('login', async (user) => { ... })
questions.explanation: addCommand extends browser or element with project-specific helpers, keeping tests concise.

questions.prompt: A suite must run on Chrome, Firefox and a mobile Safari emulator, with different specs for mobile. What WebdriverIO features help?
options: Multiple capabilities in wdio.conf with per-capability specs/exclude, plus maxInstances to run them in parallel
Running npx wdio three times manually
questions.explanation: One config can list several capabilities, each with its own spec selection, and the runner launches them in parallel workers.

questions.prompt: Your WDIO tests use `browser.pause(2000)` 150 times and take 40 minutes. What change gives the best speed and stability?
options: Replace pauses with waits on real conditions (waitForDisplayed, waitUntil, retrying expect matchers)
Increase maxInstances to 50 and keep the pauses
questions.explanation: Condition-based waits finish as soon as the app is ready and wait longer only when needed, so tests get both faster and more stable. Shorter pauses just get flakier.

coding.title: A tiny $/$$ over a fake DOM
coding.prompt:
Model WebdriverIO's selectors over a fake DOM (an array of `{ sel, text, displayed }`). Write `makeBrowser(dom)` returning an object with:

- `async $(sel)`: the first element with that `sel`, wrapped as `{ getText: async () => text, isDisplayed: async () => displayed }`; if none, an object whose `isDisplayed()` resolves to `false` and whose `getText()` rejects with `Error('element ("<sel>") still not existing')`.
- `async $$(sel)`: an array of wrappers for all matches (possibly empty).
coding.explanation: Like WebdriverIO, a missing element from $ is not an immediate error: you get an object you can still query (isDisplayed is false), and only an action that needs the element fails. $$ returns an empty array when nothing matches, the usual way to assert absence.
hints: Write a wrap(el) helper returning the two async methods.
$ uses dom.find; $$ uses dom.filter and maps through wrap.
For a missing element, return an object whose getText throws.

tests.name: $ finds first match
tests.code: const b = makeBrowser([{sel:'.item', text:'Mug', displayed:true},{sel:'.item', text:'Pen', displayed:true}]); assertEqual(await (await b.$('.item')).getText(), 'Mug')

tests.name: $$ returns all and empty
tests.code: const b = makeBrowser([{sel:'.item', text:'Mug', displayed:true},{sel:'.item', text:'Pen', displayed:false}]); const all = await b.$$('.item'); assertEqual(await Promise.all(all.map(e => e.getText())), ['Mug','Pen']); assertEqual((await b.$$('.none')).length, 0)

tests.name: missing element behaviour
tests.code: const b = makeBrowser([]); const el = await b.$('#x'); assertEqual(await el.isDisplayed(), false); let m=''; try { await el.getText(); } catch(e) { m = e.message; } assertEqual(m, 'element ("#x") still not existing')

coding.title: Add a custom command
coding.explanation: Binding this to the target lets a command use other browser methods (this.url, this.$), which is how WebdriverIO custom commands compose. Refusing to overwrite existing names protects built-in commands from being replaced by accident (WebdriverIO uses overwriteCommand for deliberate overrides).
hints: Use the `in` operator to check for an existing property.
Assign a function that calls fn.apply(target, args).
Return fn's result so async commands can be awaited.

tests.name: binds this and passes args
tests.code: const b = { base: 'https://x.test' }; addCommand(b, 'open', function (p) { return this.base + p; }); assertEqual(b.open('/cart'), 'https://x.test/cart')

tests.name: async commands
tests.code: const b = { user: 'ana' }; addCommand(b, 'login', async function (pw) { return this.user + ':' + pw.length; }); assertEqual(await b.login('secret'), 'ana:6')

tests.name: refuses to overwrite
tests.code: const b = { click() {} }; let m=''; try { addCommand(b, 'click', () => 1); } catch(e) { m = e.message; } assertEqual(m, 'command exists: click')
